title: Andaman & Nicobar Islands Travel Guide: Islands, Marine Life, History & How Travel Really Works
content:
Introduction

The Andaman & Nicobar Islands are often reduced to postcard images — white sand, turquoise water, leaning palms.

But travel here is shaped less by beaches and more by geography. This is an archipelago in the Bay of Bengal where distances are measured by sea routes, ferries replace highways, marine parks regulate access, and weather quietly influences daily plans.

Planning Andaman is different from planning mainland India. You don’t rush through it. You move with it.

This guide explains how the islands are structured, how travel works, what each major region offers, and how to approach your trip realistically.

Location & Regional Structure

The Andaman & Nicobar Islands lie roughly 1,200 km from mainland India in the Bay of Bengal.

Tourism is concentrated in the Andaman group, particularly South Andaman. The Nicobar Islands, though part of the same administrative territory, are largely restricted and not open for regular tourism.

The main entry point is Sri Vijaya Puram (formerly Port Blair) in South Andaman. From here, movement between islands happens via ferry. There are no bridges connecting islands.

Important to Understand Early

Islands are separated by sea routes. Overpacking your itinerary without accounting for ferry schedules often leads to rushed travel and missed connections.

How Travel Works Here

Inter-island travel depends almost entirely on sea routes. Private high-speed ferries operate between major islands.

Private Ferry Operators

  • Makruzz
  • Nautika
  • Green Ocean

Typical Ferry Durations

  • Sri Vijaya Puram → Swaraj Dweep: 1.5–2.5 hours
  • Sri Vijaya Puram → Shaheed Dweep: 1–1.5 hours
  • Swaraj Dweep → Shaheed Dweep: 45–60 minutes

Ferry schedules are influenced by sea conditions. Morning departures are common, and same-day back-and-forth island hopping is rarely practical.

Buffer Time Recommendation

Always keep buffer time before departure flights. Weather-related delays are not unusual, especially outside peak season.

Major Islands at a Glance

Sri Vijaya Puram (Port Blair)

The capital and administrative centre.

  • Cellular Jail
  • Aberdeen Bazaar
  • Corbyn’s Cove
  • North Bay Island (₹20 note lighthouse)
  • WWII-era Japanese bunkers

Suggested Stay: 1–2 nights

Swaraj Dweep (Havelock Island)

The most visited island in the Andamans.

  • Radhanagar Beach
  • Elephant Beach
  • Scuba diving & snorkelling
  • Wide stay and dining options

Suggested Stay: 2–3 nights

Shaheed Dweep (Neil Island)

Smaller and quieter.

  • Laxmanpur Beach sunsets
  • Natural Bridge rock formation
  • Open, less commercial shoreline

Suggested Stay: 1–2 nights

Baratang Island

Located between South and Middle Andaman.

  • Limestone caves
  • Mangrove creeks
  • Mud volcanoes

Access requires early morning convoy travel through protected forest areas.

Diglipur (North Andaman)

  • Ross & Smith twin islands
  • Saddle Peak trek
  • Seasonal turtle nesting beaches

Requires significant travel time and planning.

Little Andaman (Hut Bay)

  • Waterfalls
  • Surf-friendly stretches
  • Fewer crowds

Limited ferry schedules. Advance planning required.

Barren Island

India’s only active volcano.

  • Boat expeditions from Swaraj Dweep
  • No landing permitted
  • Highly weather dependent

Activities in the Andaman Islands

Water & Marine Activities

  • Scuba diving (Discovery, Open Water, Advanced, Fun Dives)
  • Snorkelling
  • Sea walk
  • Kayaking (sunrise & mangrove routes)
  • Game fishing
  • Parasailing (limited zones)
  • Glass-bottom boat rides
  • Stand-up paddle boarding
  • Barren Island expeditions
  • South Button snorkelling trips

Nature & Outdoor Experiences

  • Intertidal walks (Barmunallah, Shaheed Dweep)
  • Munda Pahad trek
  • Saddle Peak trek
  • Limestone cave exploration
  • Mangrove boat rides
  • Birdwatching at Chidiya Tapu
  • Stargazing in low light zones

Cultural & Historical Stops

  • Cellular Jail
  • Light & sound show
  • Japanese bunkers
  • Marine & anthropological museums
  • Aberdeen Bazaar

Marine activities depend heavily on sea conditions and seasonal visibility.

Cost Expectations (Broad Reference)

  • Budget stays: ₹1,200–₹3,500
  • Mid-range stays: ₹4,000–₹8,000
  • Premium stays: ₹9,000–₹20,000+
  • Introductory scuba: ₹3,500–₹6,000
  • Private ferries: ₹1,200–₹2,500
  • Barren Island expeditions: ₹20,000+ (varies)

Prices fluctuate seasonally.

Best Time to Visit

November–March

Calmer seas, clearer water, reliable ferry schedules.

April–May

Hotter but generally stable conditions.

June–September (Monsoon)

Rougher seas, possible ferry cancellations, limited marine visibility.

Who Andaman Is For

Well Suited For

  • Couples
  • Slow travellers
  • Water-focused trips
  • Nature-led holidays

Less Suited For

  • Nightlife-driven travel
  • Ultra-tight itineraries
  • Travellers uncomfortable with ferry movement

How Many Days Make Sense

  • 4–5 days: Covers Sri Vijaya Puram and Swaraj Dweep, but feels rushed.
  • 6–7 days: Balanced first trip including Shaheed Dweep.
  • 8–10 days: Comfortable pacing with scope for Baratang or Little Andaman.
  • 10+ days: Allows North Andaman or specialised expeditions.

Final Perspective

The Andaman Islands reward travellers who allow time between ferries, avoid stacking activities, and let evenings remain unplanned.

Approach them like a checklist destination and they will feel fragmented.

Approach them patiently and they feel expansive.

title: Barren Island: India’s Only Active Volcano — What the Trip Is Really Like
content:
🌋 Introduction

Barren Island sits alone in the Andaman Sea.

There are no settlements. No jetty. No beach shacks. No landing permission.

It is India’s only active volcano.

Visiting it is not a casual day trip — it is a full marine expedition that begins before sunrise and depends entirely on sea conditions.

For many travellers, this becomes the most memorable day of the Andaman journey.

📍 Where Barren Island Is Located

Barren Island lies approximately 135 km northeast of Sri Vijaya Puram.

Most expeditions depart from:

  • Swaraj Dweep
  • Occasionally Sri Vijaya Puram

Travel time by speedboat is usually 3–4 hours each way depending on sea state.

There are no scheduled ferries. Only licensed expedition boats operate this route.

🚤 The Departure

Barren Island days begin early.

Most boats depart before sunrise to allow:

  • Sufficient daylight
  • Safer sea conditions
  • Return before evening

You board a speedboat with a small group and move quickly into deeper sea. The coastline disappears fast.

🌫️ What You See on Arrival

As you approach, the shoreline turns black and rugged. The volcanic cone rises sharply from the sea.

Depending on activity levels, faint smoke may be visible from the crater.

Landing is not permitted. Boats circle at a regulated distance.

The atmosphere feels heavier and more elemental than beach islands.

🤿 Snorkelling & Diving Near Barren Island

Many expeditions include snorkelling or diving stops near reef zones around the island.

The water can be exceptionally clear.

Marine life may include:

  • Reef fish
  • Coral formations
  • Occasional pelagic species

Depth and visibility vary depending on sea conditions.

Diving here is typically reserved for certified divers.

💰 Cost & What to Expect

This is not a budget activity.

Expeditions usually range between ₹25,000–₹40,000+ per person depending on:

  • Departure island
  • Boat type
  • Inclusion of snorkelling or diving
  • Fuel costs

Weather plays a decisive role. If sea conditions are unsafe, departures may be cancelled — sometimes on the morning of travel.

Flexibility is essential.

🌊 What the Ride Feels Like

The outbound journey can feel long.

On calm days, it’s smooth. On windy days, movement is noticeable.

You are far from shore with no midway stops. This is open-sea travel — not coastal hopping.

If prone to motion sickness, preparation helps.

🛑 Safety & Permissions

  • Landing is prohibited
  • Boats maintain regulated distance
  • Trips operate under licensed operators

Even when volcanic activity is minimal, the terrain remains unstable.

This is observation, not exploration.

📅 Best Time to Visit

November to April:

  • Calmer seas
  • Stronger visibility
  • Higher departure reliability

Monsoon months (June–September) see reduced departures due to rough waters.

🤔 Is It Worth It?

Barren Island is not for everyone.

It isn’t comfortable like beaches. It isn’t social like café evenings.

It is elemental.

You leave land before sunrise, cross open sea, circle a volcanic island, snorkel in deeper waters, and return by late afternoon.

For some travellers, this becomes the defining memory of the Andamans.

🎒 Practical Advice

  • Book only through licensed operators
  • Keep a buffer day in case of cancellation
  • Carry sun protection and water
  • Wear non-slip footwear
  • Prepare for full-day exposure

This is an expedition, not an excursion.

title: Sri Vijaya Puram (Port Blair) Travel Guide: History, Things to Do, Food, Stays & Transport
content:
Introduction

Sri Vijaya Puram, formerly known as Port Blair, is where every Andaman journey begins.

Flights arrive here. Ferries depart from here. Permits, transfers, and inter-island movement flow through this administrative centre before travellers step onto other islands.

While often treated as a short transit stop, the city holds historical, political, and logistical significance that shapes the rest of the archipelago experience.

Location and Role

Sri Vijaya Puram lies in South Andaman and functions as the capital of the Andaman & Nicobar Islands.

  • Veer Savarkar International Airport
  • Haddo Jetty and Phoenix Bay Jetty
  • Administrative and government offices

Most itineraries begin or conclude here with one to two nights allocated for orientation and logistics.

Historical Context

The Cellular Jail stands as the most significant historical structure in the islands. Built by the British, it was designed for solitary confinement of political prisoners.

Today it functions as a national memorial, with an evening light-and-sound program that contextualises the freedom struggle.

During World War II, Japanese forces occupied the Andaman Islands between 1942 and 1945.

Remnants of wartime bunkers still exist along parts of the coastline. Nearby Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose Island carries visible ruins from both British and Japanese periods.

Places to Visit

Cellular Jail

The defining landmark of the city and an essential visit for first-time travellers.

Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose Island

  • British-era ruins intertwined with tree roots
  • Harbour viewpoints
  • Japanese occupation remnants

North Bay Island

Known for snorkelling and sea walk experiences. The lighthouse appears on the reverse side of the Indian ₹20 note.

Corbyn’s Cove Beach

Located close to the city centre, suitable for evening walks and seasonal water sports.

Aberdeen Bazaar

The primary market area offering local bakeries, small eateries, souvenir shops, and everyday island commerce.

Things to Do

Historical and Cultural

  • Explore Cellular Jail
  • Attend the evening light-and-sound show
  • Visit the Anthropological and Samudrika Marine Museums
  • Walk along Japanese bunker stretches

Coastal and Nature

  • Snorkelling and sea walk at North Bay
  • Water sports at Corbyn’s Cove
  • Sunset at Chidiya Tapu
  • Munda Pahad Trek
  • Intertidal exploration at Barmunallah

Marine activities around Sri Vijaya Puram are limited compared to Swaraj Dweep. Most advanced diving is centred there.

Food and Cafés

Sri Vijaya Puram offers the widest dining range in the Andamans.

  • Local bakeries near Aberdeen Bazaar
  • Harbour-side coffee shops
  • Seafood-focused restaurants
  • Waterfront dining in premium hotels

Dining hours are generally earlier than mainland cities.

Stay Options

Budget (Under ₹4,000)

  • Hotel Driftwood
  • Ansha Residency

Mid-Range (₹4,000–₹8,000)

  • Hotel Shompen
  • Symphony Samudra

Premium (₹9,000+)

  • Seashell Port Blair
  • Silver Sand Sentinel

Peak season increases rates significantly.

Getting Around

Local Transport

Private taxis are widely available. Auto rickshaws operate on shorter routes within city limits.

Bike Rentals

Motorbike rentals range between ₹400–₹700 per day. Refuelling before longer drives is advisable.

Transfers

Most hotels arrange airport and jetty transfers on request. Early ferry departures require coordination.

How Many Days to Spend

One day is sufficient for orientation and Cellular Jail.

Two days allow inclusion of nearby islands and coastal extensions.

More than two days typically makes sense only when adding Baratang or deeper exploration.

Practical Notes

  • Carry valid ID for ferry bookings
  • Connectivity is stronger here than on outer islands
  • ATMs are more reliable than elsewhere in the archipelago
  • Start early for Baratang convoys

title: Shaheed Dweep (Neil Island) Travel Guide: Beaches, Quiet Stays, Food & Island Rhythm
content:
🌿 Introduction

Shaheed Dweep — still called Neil Island by most travellers — feels different the moment you arrive.

The jetty is smaller. The roads are flatter. There are fewer cafés, fewer vehicles, fewer people moving in a hurry.

Where Swaraj Dweep revolves around diving schedules and sunset crowds, Shaheed Dweep moves at a quieter pace.

It isn’t an island of activities. It’s an island of space.

🚢 Reaching Shaheed Dweep

Shaheed Dweep lies between Sri Vijaya Puram and Swaraj Dweep.

Ferry duration:

  • ⏱️ Around 1–1.5 hours from Sri Vijaya Puram
  • ⏱️ Around 45–60 minutes from Swaraj Dweep

Arrivals are usually smooth. Transfers take 10–15 minutes to most properties.

Because distances are small, many travellers underestimate how much calmer the island feels compared to Havelock.

🏖️ The Beaches

🌊 Bharatpur Beach

Closest to the jetty, Bharatpur has shallow waters that remain relatively calm during stable months.

It’s the most activity-oriented beach on the island, with occasional snorkelling and glass-bottom boat operations.

Morning visits work best before the sun grows strong.

🌅 Laxmanpur Beach

Long and open, Laxmanpur is more about shoreline walks than swimming.

Evenings here are quieter than Radhanagar in Swaraj Dweep. Sunsets stretch wide without crowd buildup.

This is the beach most people remember.

🪨 Natural Bridge (Howrah Bridge)

Best visited during low tide, this natural rock formation arches over the shoreline.

Small marine life becomes visible in shallow pools nearby.

⏰ Tide timings are essential for visiting the Natural Bridge. Plan around low tide.

🚲 What You Actually Do Here

Shaheed Dweep is not packed with scheduled activities.

You wake up slower. You ride to a beach without checking the clock. You return before dark without much traffic.

Experiences include:

  • 🤿 Snorkelling near Bharatpur when sea conditions permit
  • 🌊 Intertidal exploration near the Natural Bridge
  • 🚲 Cycling along flat interior roads
  • 🌄 Early morning walks along Laxmanpur

Compared to Swaraj Dweep, marine activities are limited and lower intensity.

The island rewards unplanned hours.

🍽️ Food & Small Cafés

The food scene here is smaller and more relaxed.

Many restaurants are attached to stays rather than standalone cafés.

Regularly visited places include:

  • Garden View Restaurant
  • Sea Zaika
  • Small family-run cafés near Bharatpur

Menus depend on availability. Seafood is seasonal. Evenings are quiet.

Dining here feels local rather than curated.

🏨 Where to Stay

📍 Bharatpur Side

Closest to the jetty. Convenient for short stays.

Budget to Mid-Range (₹2,500–₹6,000)

  • Hotel Pearl Park
  • Summer Sands Beach Resort

🌇 Laxmanpur Side

Quieter and better for sunset access.

Mid-Range to Premium (₹5,000–₹12,000)

  • SeaShell Neil
  • Silver Sand Beach Resort (Neil)

Unlike Swaraj Dweep, there are fewer high-end resort options.

Advance bookings are recommended during peak season as inventory is limited.

🛵 Getting Around

Scooters and bicycles are the easiest way to move around.

Rental rates generally range from ₹400–₹600 per day depending on season.

Distances between beaches are short, and roads are mostly flat.

Night movement is minimal. Most activity winds down soon after sunset.

⏳ How Long to Stay

Many travellers arrive after two or three nights in Swaraj Dweep.

  • 🗓️ One night gives a quick look at the beaches.
  • 🌅 Two nights allow the island to feel slower and less scheduled.

Longer stays are usually intentional slow travel.

🗺️ Where It Sits in the Journey

A typical route flows like this:

Sri Vijaya Puram → Swaraj Dweep → Shaheed Dweep → Return

If Swaraj Dweep feels structured and active, Shaheed Dweep softens the pace before returning to ferry schedules.

It is less about doing more — and more about doing less.

📝 Practical Notes

  • 🌊 Tide timings matter for the Natural Bridge
  • 📶 Mobile connectivity can fluctuate outside central areas
  • 💵 Carry sufficient cash — ATM options are limited
  • ⛴️ Plan ferry departures with buffer time

title: First Time in the Andaman Islands: How to Plan Your Trip Right
content:
Introduction

Planning a first trip to the Andaman Islands often feels straightforward at first glance. The islands appear close to one another, distances seem short, and most itineraries online look manageable within five or six days.

In practice, travel here moves to a different rhythm.

Inter-island movement depends on ferries. Activity schedules depend on sea conditions. Even hotel transfers require planning because islands are not built like compact mainland towns.

This guide focuses on what matters for a first visit: duration, island selection, ferry logic, activity planning, and cost structure — so that the trip feels measured rather than compressed.

How Many Days Make Sense

Four to five days allows a visit to Sri Vijaya Puram and Swaraj Dweep. It is workable, but movement will occupy a significant portion of the schedule. Arrival, one ferry transfer, and departure planning leave limited flexibility for unplanned time.

Six to seven days creates a more balanced structure. You can spend time in Sri Vijaya Puram without rushing through it, move to Swaraj Dweep with a full evening available, and add Shaheed Dweep without reducing it to a brief stop.

Eight days or more allows additional regions such as Baratang to be included without disrupting the flow of the trip.

North Andaman requires substantial road travel and is better suited to longer itineraries.

Choosing Islands for a First Visit

For most first-time travellers, two or three islands are sufficient.

Sri Vijaya Puram functions as the entry and exit point and provides historical context through sites such as the Cellular Jail, Aberdeen Bazaar, and nearby coastal stretches.

Swaraj Dweep is typically the longest stay. It combines beaches, marine activities, and the widest range of accommodation.

Shaheed Dweep offers a quieter setting with shorter internal travel distances and open shorelines.

Extending beyond this increases transit time significantly.

Ferry Planning and Inter Island Transfers

Ferry operators include:

  • Makruzz
  • Nautika
  • Green Ocean

Most sailings operate in the morning or early afternoon.

Ferry days should be treated as transition days. Even when travel time is under two hours, reporting time, boarding, luggage handling, and hotel transfers reduce usable hours.

Avoid planning major marine activities immediately after arriving on a new island.

Similarly, avoid returning to Sri Vijaya Puram on the same morning as a departure flight.

Planning Activities Thoughtfully

Marine activities depend on weather and sea state.

Common options include:

  • Introductory scuba diving
  • Certified diving courses
  • Snorkelling trips
  • Sea walk experiences
  • Kayaking in mangroves
  • Intertidal walks
  • Boat-based excursions such as Barren Island

It is advisable to schedule one primary marine activity per day. This provides flexibility in case of rescheduling and prevents fatigue.

Budget: What Actually Drives the Cost

1. Flights

Airfare varies significantly by season and departure city. During peak months, fares increase sharply. Early booking helps.

2. Accommodation

Accommodation ranges broadly:

  • Budget guesthouses: ₹1,200–₹3,500 per night
  • Mid-range hotels and beach stays: ₹4,000–₹8,000
  • Premium resorts: ₹9,000–₹20,000+

Room rates increase in peak season and during long weekends.

3. Ferry Transfers

Private ferry tickets typically range between ₹1,200–₹2,500 per sector. Multiple island transfers increase total cost.

Government ferries are less expensive but less predictable in terms of availability and comfort.

4. Marine Activities

This is where expenditure increases most.

Introductory scuba diving sessions generally range between ₹3,500–₹6,000.

Certified dive courses cost significantly more depending on certification level.

Snorkelling trips, sea walk experiences, kayaking, and specialised excursions are additional expenses ranging from ₹1,000 to ₹3,500

Barren Island expeditions operate at a higher price range and are subject to weather approvals with typically a shared charter would cost ₹25,000 per person to a private charter starting from ₹1,50,000

When multiple marine activities are added within a short itinerary, activity costs can exceed accommodation expenses.

5. Local Transport

Bike rentals on Swaraj Dweep and Shaheed Dweep usually range between ₹500–₹700 per day.

Private taxis in Sri Vijaya Puram vary by distance.

Fuel stations are limited on smaller islands, so planning refuelling in advance is advisable.

6. Miscellaneous

Entry permits, local transfers, light-and-sound show tickets, and small daily expenses accumulate gradually.

Understanding that marine experiences form the largest variable cost helps create a realistic estimate before finalising plans.

Best Time for a First Visit

November to March offers the most stable conditions for first-time travellers. Sea state is calmer and ferry reliability is higher.

April and May are warmer but manageable.

Monsoon months (June to September) bring increased variability in sea conditions and activity schedules.

Structuring the Trip

A simple structure works well:

  • Arrival day reserved for light exploration.
  • Dedicated ferry days without major activities.
  • One primary activity per island.
  • A buffer before departure.

This approach keeps transitions manageable.

Final Perspective

The Andaman Islands reward measured planning.

When ferry movement, activity scheduling, and budget allocation are considered early, the trip feels cohesive. When transitions are compressed, logistics begin to dominate the experience.

For a first visit, clarity and spacing create the strongest introduction to the islands.

title: Swaraj Dweep (Havelock Island) Travel Guide: Beaches, Diving, Food, Stays & How the Island Actually Works
content:
Introduction

Swaraj Dweep, still widely called Havelock Island, is where most Andaman trips settle into rhythm.

You arrive by ferry. The jetty feels busier than the rest of the islands. Dive shops line the main road. Scooters outnumber taxis.

Unlike Sri Vijaya Puram, which functions as a transit point, Swaraj Dweep is where travellers stay longer — not because there is more to cover, but because the pace allows space between activities.

Reef mornings, forest roads, and long sunsets shape the structure of days here.

Reaching Swaraj Dweep

Swaraj Dweep lies approximately 1.5 to 2.5 hours by ferry from Sri Vijaya Puram.

Private ferry operators include:

  • Makruzz
  • Nautika
  • Green Ocean

Most sailings operate in the morning or early afternoon.

Arrival days are best kept light. Avoid scheduling diving or long activities immediately after ferry transfer.

The Beaches

Radhanagar Beach

Radhanagar is often the defining image of the island. The shoreline is wide, the sand fine, and forest sits directly behind the beach without construction interrupting the horizon.

Late afternoons draw visitors for sunset. It is not activity-focused — it is a beach for open space and stillness.

Elephant Beach

Elephant Beach is activity-driven. The reef sits closer to shore, making snorkelling accessible.

Most visitors reach it by boat. Sea conditions determine accessibility and timing.

Kala Pathar Beach

Located on the eastern edge of the island, Kala Pathar feels quieter.

Darker rock formations shape the coastline, and early mornings are typically calm.

Diving and Marine Life

Swaraj Dweep is the diving centre of the Andaman Islands. Dive shops line Govind Nagar, and boats depart early each morning toward reef sites.

Available options include:

  • Discovery scuba dives for beginners
  • Open Water and Advanced certifications
  • Fun dives for certified divers
  • Snorkelling sessions
  • Mangrove kayaking

Introductory dive sessions typically range between ₹3,500–₹6,000 depending on operator and season.

Schedule one primary marine activity per day to allow flexibility for sea conditions and rescheduling.

Food and Cafés

Govind Nagar functions as the informal dining centre of the island.

Breakfast cafés open early for divers, and seafood menus depend on daily catch.

Commonly visited cafés and restaurants include:

  • Full Moon Café
  • Something Different
  • Anju Coco
  • Bonova Café & Pub
  • Fat Martin Café
  • Nemo Café

Nights remain intentionally quiet compared to mainland destinations.

Where to Stay

Govind Nagar

Closest to the jetty and dive centres. Suitable for short stays and activity-focused itineraries.

  • Budget: Emerald Gecko, Blue Bird Resort
  • Mid-Range: TSG Blue, Symphony Palms

Radhanagar Side

Quieter and more scenic. Properties focus on space and surroundings.

  • Taj Exotica Resort & Spa
  • Barefoot at Havelock

Kala Pathar Side

Less traffic, fewer shops, more privacy.

  • Havelock Island Beach Resort
  • SeaShell Havelock

Prices fluctuate significantly between peak season (November–March) and monsoon months.

Getting Around

Scooters are the primary mode of transport. Rental rates generally range between ₹400–₹700 per day.

Fuel stations are limited. Refuel before travelling toward Radhanagar or Kala Pathar.

Roads are narrow and forest-lined. Night riding requires caution.

How Long to Stay

One night largely revolves around ferry timings.

Two nights allow one full activity morning and a complete sunset cycle.

Three nights or more create flexibility for diving courses or a slower pace.

Where It Fits in an Itinerary

Most first-time routes follow this structure:

  • Sri Vijaya Puram
  • Swaraj Dweep
  • Shaheed Dweep
  • Return to Sri Vijaya Puram

Swaraj Dweep functions as the active middle segment — reef mornings, scooter afternoons, and extended beach evenings.

Practical Notes

  • Mobile connectivity fluctuates outside central stretches
  • ATMs are limited — carry backup cash
  • Elephant Beach access depends on sea behaviour
  • Book dive sessions early during peak season

title: Best Time to Visit the Andaman Islands: Weather, Sea Conditions & Travel Seasons Explained
content:
Introduction

In the Andaman Islands, the question is not “summer or winter?”

It is “how is the sea behaving?”

Unlike most mainland destinations, travel here is shaped less by temperature and more by water conditions. Ferry reliability, underwater visibility, activity operations, and even island accessibility change with season.

If this is your first visit, understanding seasonality will influence more than just comfort — it will influence how your itinerary unfolds.

Understanding Andaman’s Climate Pattern

The Andaman Islands follow a tropical maritime climate. Temperatures remain relatively stable throughout the year, typically between 23°C and 32°C.

What changes significantly is:

  • Wind speed
  • Sea state
  • Rainfall intensity
  • Underwater visibility

Instead of thinking in traditional four seasons, it helps to break the year into four functional travel phases.

November to March — The Most Stable Window

This is widely considered the most reliable period to visit.

What Conditions Are Typically Like

  • Calmer seas
  • Higher underwater visibility
  • More predictable ferry schedules
  • Lower humidity compared to peak monsoon

For first-time visitors, this window reduces uncertainty.

Scuba diving visibility is generally stronger during these months, particularly around Swaraj Dweep. Boat-based excursions such as Barren Island are more consistently operational (weather still applies).

What to Expect

This is also peak season.

  • Higher hotel tariffs
  • Advance ferry bookings required
  • Popular stays sell out early

If you are planning between December and February, booking well in advance is advisable.

April and May — Warmer but Still Workable

April and May are hotter months.

Sea conditions are often still stable, but daytime heat increases noticeably.

What Changes

  • Midday sun is intense
  • Outdoor movement is best early morning or late afternoon
  • Water remains clear for marine activities

This period can still work well if you plan activity-heavy mornings and slower afternoons.

Hotel pricing may begin to soften slightly compared to winter peak.

June to September — Monsoon Period

Monsoon in Andaman is different from mainland hill-station rain.

The impact is primarily on the sea.

What Typically Changes

  • Rougher waters
  • Occasional ferry cancellations
  • Reduced underwater visibility
  • Some marine activities paused depending on conditions

It is still possible to travel during monsoon, particularly if you are based in Sri Vijaya Puram and keeping plans flexible.

However, if your trip centres around scuba diving, snorkelling, or boat-based excursions, monsoon increases unpredictability.

This season suits travellers who are comfortable adjusting plans in real time.

October — Transition Phase

October marks the gradual shift out of monsoon.

Sea conditions begin stabilising, but variability can continue early in the month.

By late October:

  • Ferry schedules improve
  • Marine activities resume more consistently
  • Crowd levels remain moderate

This can be a balanced time for travellers seeking fewer peak-season crowds.

How Seasonality Affects Specific Activities

Scuba Diving

Underwater visibility is generally strongest between November and May.

During monsoon months, visibility may reduce depending on rainfall and sediment movement.

Ferry Movement

Ferry reliability is highest in winter months. Rough seas during monsoon can result in schedule adjustments.

Barren Island

Excursions depend heavily on weather approvals and sea state. Winter months provide higher consistency.

Beach Time

Beaches remain accessible year-round, but swimming advisories depend on tidal and wind conditions.

Crowd & Pricing Patterns

Peak Season (Dec–Feb)

  • Highest hotel rates
  • Advance bookings required
  • More visitors on popular beaches

Shoulder (Oct, April)

  • Moderate pricing
  • Balanced crowd levels

Monsoon (June–Sept)

  • Lower tariffs
  • Fewer visitors
  • Greater flexibility required

Understanding this helps you align expectations with budget.

So, When Is the Best Time?

For a first-time traveller planning marine activities and island hopping, November to March provides the most stable introduction.

If you are comfortable with heat, April and May remain workable.

If you prioritise quieter surroundings and flexible travel, monsoon months can still be meaningful — provided expectations are adjusted.

There is no universally “perfect” month.

There is only the month that aligns with what you want from the islands.

title: How to Book Ferries in the Andaman Islands: Routes, Operators, Timing & Common Mistakes
content:
Introduction

Ferries in the Andaman Islands aren’t just transport — they quietly shape your trip.

Arrival times determine when you check in. Departure times decide how early you wake up. Sea conditions influence your schedule more than road traffic ever would on the mainland.

Understanding ferry movement early makes the rest of your planning easier.

🚢 What Ferry Days Actually Feel Like

Most inter-island travel happens in the morning or early afternoon.

You’ll usually arrive at the jetty 45–60 minutes before departure. Luggage is tagged and stored separately. Boarding happens in batches. Cabins are air-conditioned and seated.

During stable sea months, crossings feel smooth. On rougher days, movement is noticeable but manageable.

It isn’t dramatic — but it’s not like boarding a flight either. There’s more flexibility and more dependence on sea conditions.

🗺️ Main Ferry Routes

Sri Vijaya Puram ↔ Swaraj Dweep

Approx. 1.5–2.5 hours

The busiest and most frequently used tourist route.

Sri Vijaya Puram ↔ Shaheed Dweep

Approx. 1–1.5 hours

Shorter sailing, typically with morning departures.

Swaraj Dweep ↔ Shaheed Dweep

Approx. 45–60 minutes

Common mid-trip transition.

Longer northern routes such as Diglipur and Mayabunder operate less frequently and require advance planning.

🏝️ Jetties & Boarding Environment

You’ll typically depart from:

  • Phoenix Bay Jetty
  • Haddo Jetty

These are functional terminals rather than large transit hubs. During peak season, they can feel crowded but move at a steady pace.

Arriving too early isn’t necessary. Arriving too late creates avoidable stress.

⛴️ Ferry Operators

Private ferries dominate tourist routes:

  • Makruzz
  • Nautika
  • Green Ocean

These generally offer fixed seating, air-conditioned cabins, and faster travel times.

Government ferries operate on select routes. They are slower, more basic, and commonly used by locals.

📅 When to Book

Peak season (November–March) sees higher demand, especially for morning sailings.

  • Book inter-island ferries once travel dates are confirmed
  • Avoid scheduling ferry arrivals and major activities on the same morning
  • Keep a buffer before departure flights

Sea delays are uncommon but possible. Always leave a safety margin before flights.

⏰ How Ferry Timing Shapes Your Day

Most ferries depart between 6:30 AM and 2:00 PM.

Early departures mean:

  • Pre-sunrise wake-up
  • Minimal breakfast time

Midday arrivals mean:

  • Half your day is already gone
  • Limited scope for water activities

Ferry days are best treated as transition days rather than activity-heavy ones.

💰 Approximate Cost Range

Private ferry tickets typically range between ₹1,200–₹2,500 depending on:

  • Route
  • Operator
  • Season

Premium seat categories may cost slightly more. Prices fluctuate during peak months.

🌊 Weather & Sea Conditions

Between November and March, seas are generally calmer.

During monsoon months (June–September):

  • Sailings may be rescheduled
  • Routes may operate less frequently

The sea determines more than the schedule.

⚠️ Common Mistakes

  • Booking ferry return too close to flight departure
  • Planning scuba diving on arrival morning
  • Assuming ferries operate exactly like airlines
  • Scheduling back-to-back ferry days

Limiting island changes to two or three across the entire trip makes the journey smoother.

🎒 What to Carry on Ferry Day

  • Government-issued ID
  • Light jacket (cabins can be cold)
  • Motion sickness medication if needed
  • Water and small snacks

Luggage is typically stored separately from passenger seating.

Final Perspective

In the Andamans, ferries don’t just connect islands — they shape how the islands are experienced.

Planning with sea routes in mind keeps your trip balanced. More islands don’t always mean more experiences.

Sometimes fewer crossings lead to better days.
